Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) has lifted its S&P 500 targets and earnings forecasts, driven by a combination of lower-than-expected tariffs, improved economic growth, and reduced recession risks.

The bank now sees the benchmark index reaching 6100 by year-end and 6500 in 12 months, up from prior forecasts of 5900 and 6200.

The Wall Street firm lifted its 2025 and 2026 S&P 500 earnings per share (EPS) growth estimates to 7% in both years, compared to earlier projections of 3% and 6%.
